events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 534 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near Savannah River Site, moving north at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

This tornadic thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
west central Barnwell and south central Aiken Counties, including the
following locations... Savannah River Site K Complex.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL out 20
NM...
Waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 615 PM EDT.

* At 535 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 8 nm east of Jacksonville Beach, or 24 nm
north of Saint Augustine, moving northeast at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Anna Reef.

events.region: Monroe Upper Keys; Monroe Middle Keys; Monroe Lower Keys
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets and
lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater. In addition, in the Upper
Keys, Bayside communities will likely see little to no relief
from flooding even at low tide.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 533 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 4.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
North Augusta, Augusta, Fort Gordon, Clearwater, Belvedere,
Hephzibah, South Augusta, Glendale, Daniel Field, Summerville,
Midtown, Augusta Mall, Augusta Regional Airport, Augusta National
Golf Club, Village Plaza Shopping Center, McBean, Gloverville and
Burnettown.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 520 in South Carolina between mile markers 16 and 23.
Interstate 20 in South Carolina between mile markers 0 and 7.
Interstate 20 in Georgia between mile markers 195 and 201. Interstate
520 in Georgia between mile markers 1 and 15.

Emigration Canyon, East Canyon State Park, Canyon Rim, Millcreek,

between mile markers 114 and 119...and between mile markers 123 and
126. Interstate 15 between mile markers 303 and 319.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Madison; Yancey; Mitchell; Swain; Haywood; Buncombe; Graham; Northern Jackson; Macon; Southern Jackson; Transylvania
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the High Wind Warning at elevations above 3500 feet,
southeast winds 10 to 25 mph with gusts up to 60 mph. For the Wind
Advisory in effect below 3500 feet, southeast winds 5 to 20 mph
with gusts up to 50 mph.

* WHERE...Most of the mountains of western North Carolina, from
Graham and Macon counties northeast to Mitchell County.

* WHEN...Until 8 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines
especially in higher elevations. Widespread power outages are
expected in higher elevations. Travel will be difficult, especially
for high profile vehicles. Gusty winds will blow around unsecured
objects, and may cause a few tree limbs to fall and cause isolated
power outages in lower elevations.

possible. A few locations could briefly gust to 45 mph.

* WHERE...Northeast Georgia, western Upstate South Carolina, plus
Avery and Henderson Counties in North Carolina, and the mountain
portions of Polk, Rutherford, McDowell, Burke, and Caldwell

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree

also could topple if rooted in saturated soil.
